## Summary

Research confidence is **Moderate**. Some of this break's ideal conditions are confirmed by sources; others rest on limited evidence. It is the class the app computes from the evidence (how well the break's ideal conditions are documented), not a forecast and not a probability.

Main gaps:

- Limited information is available about this break's preferred tide conditions.
- Limited information is available about the shape of the bottom at this break.
- Limited information is available about the swell period this break needs.
- No survey, scientific or official source confirms the best swell direction.

Research notes (research_evidence.json):

> Five readable sources from five publishers: Surf-Forecast, Wikipedia, WannaSurf, Surf Atlas and Swellnet. Stormrider's Southwest Coast region page was read but does not mention North Point, and the Wikipedia Capes surfing-locations list gives only its location; neither was recorded. No peer-reviewed, official or survey source was found. Crossref returned nothing for Gracetown, Cowaramup Bay or Margaret River surf breaks. The Ngari Capes Marine Park documents cited by Wikipedia (fish.wa.gov.au FAQ, UWA PDF) and margaretriver.com did not respond, and the Busselton Mail and Yahoo articles are gone (404). Wind: Surf-Forecast ENE (67.5) and WannaSurf SE/E (112.5) both agree with the profile's 80. A Swellnet contest forecast (2018) says S/SE and SSE winds favour North Point, which suggests the usable wind range reaches further south than 80. It does not use the words offshore or best, so it has no value. Stormrider Surf Guides' North Point page (stormrider.surf/break/north-point-1) holds 'Easterly' wind, 4-15 ft, S-W swell and mid-to-high tide. That matches the profile exactly, so the profile may come from it. Those values are only in the page's script data, which the excerpt checker cannot see, so they were not recorded. Swell direction: SW everywhere (Surf-Forecast, Surf Atlas). WannaSurf's template also lists NW and W. Size: WannaSurf's template minimum (6-8 ft, with 'Dont bother unless everywhere else is big') is above the profile's 4 ft. Surf Atlas says it holds double to triple overhead (about 12-18 ft faces, my conversion), near the profile's 15 ft. Period: no source gives a number; Surf-Forecast says groundswell. Tide: only WannaSurf (mid to high, agrees). Seasonality conflict: Surf-Forecast and Surf Atlas both point to winter. The profile's best months (Mar-Jun, Sep-Oct) share only June with winter. WannaSurf and Surf-Forecast are undated; Wikipedia is 2026, Surf Atlas 2024 and Swellnet 2018.

## Ideal conditions

Directions are compass degrees the swell or wind comes FROM, ranges clockwise. Heights keep the scale each source states (breaking face, Hawaiian, swell or relative to the surfer); the app's sizes are breaking face heights in feet. Sources are numbered as in [Sources](#sources).

### Swell height

| Field | Research value | Status | Sources | App model setting |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Minimum suitable | 6–8 ft | documented | S3 | `wave_height_min_ft` 4 ft (breaking face) |
| Ideal range | — | not documented | — | no separate setting; working range 4–15 ft |
| Maximum suitable | double to triple overhead (holds) · surfer heights (face) | documented | S3, S4 | `wave_height_max_ft` 15 ft (breaking face) |

Notes:

- **Minimum suitable**: WannaSurf says it starts working at 2-2.5 m / 6-8 ft and adds 'Dont bother unless everywhere else is big'; the template does not say whether this is face or offshore swell height.
  - S3 (WannaSurf): “Swell sizeStarts working at 2m-2.5m / 6ft-8ft and holds up to 4m+ / 12ft...Dont bother unless everywhere else is big.”
- **Ideal range**: No excerpt gives an ideal size.
- **Maximum suitable**: The Surf Atlas says winter SW pushes bring double and triple overheads that hold (face height relative to the surfer; the evidence file's 12-18 ft is its own conversion); WannaSurf's 'holds up to 4m+ / 12ft' is an open top bracket.
  - S4 (Surf Atlas): “Winter SW pushes here can bring double, triple overheads that hold”
  - S3 (WannaSurf): “Swell sizeStarts working at 2m-2.5m / 6ft-8ft and holds up to 4m+ / 12ft...Dont bother unless everywhere else is big.”

### Swell direction

| Field | Research value | Status | Sources | App model setting |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Ideal bearing | 225° (SW) | documented | S1, S4 | `optimal_swell_direction` 220–250° (SW to WSW, clockwise) |

Notes:

- **Ideal bearing**: Surf-Forecast gives the optimum swell angle as southwest, and the Surf Atlas says winter SW swells push into Cowaramup Bay.
  - S1 (Surf-Forecast.com): “Most of the surf here comes from groundswells and the optimum swell angle is from the southwest.”
  - S4 (Surf Atlas): “Winter SW pushes here can bring double, triple overheads that hold like a monster will ram through the opening of Cowaramup Bay”
- **Acceptable range**: WannaSurf lists northwest, west and southwest as good swell directions.
  - S3 (WannaSurf): “Good swell directionNorthWest, West, SouthWest”
- **Blocked directions**: No excerpt names blocked directions.
- **Exposure**: Surf-Forecast calls it a fairly exposed point break and the Surf Atlas says SW swells ram through the opening of Cowaramup Bay.
  - S1 (Surf-Forecast.com): “North Point in the Margarets River Area is a fairly exposed point break that has quite consistent surf.”
  - S4 (Surf Atlas): “Winter SW pushes here can bring double, triple overheads that hold like a monster will ram through the opening of Cowaramup Bay”
